[`fiber-pay`](https://github.com/RetricSu/fiber-pay) is a community-maintained
TypeScript toolchain for building and operating Fiber applications. It provides
typed RPC clients, browser and Node.js entrypoints, React components, local node
lifecycle helpers, and an automation-friendly CLI.

<Callout type="warning" title="Community SDK">
  `fiber-pay` is maintained independently of the official Fiber repository.
  Version 0.3.0 targets Fiber v0.9.0-rc7. Check the upstream release notes when
  using a different Fiber Node version.
</Callout>

## Choose an integration surface

| Package | Use it when you need |
| --- | --- |
| `@fiber-pay/sdk` | Typed RPC access and shared application primitives |
| `@fiber-pay/sdk/browser` | A browser WASM node, browser credentials, or a browser-safe RPC client |
| `@fiber-pay/sdk/node` | Node.js APIs and server-side L402 helpers |
| `@fiber-pay/react` | Hooks and components for passkey-based browser payment flows |
| `@fiber-pay/cli` | Node, channel, invoice, payment, and automation workflows from a terminal or agent |

The separate `@fiber-pay/agent` package is experimental and is not recommended
by its maintainer for production use.

## Connect to a Fiber Node

Install the core SDK:

```bash
npm install @fiber-pay/sdk
```

Create a typed RPC client that points to a node you control:

```typescript
import { FiberRpcClient } from "@fiber-pay/sdk";

const client = new FiberRpcClient({
  url: "http://127.0.0.1:8227",
  biscuitToken: process.env.FIBER_RPC_BISCUIT_TOKEN,
});

const info = await client.nodeInfo();
console.log(info.pubkey);
```

Keep privileged Biscuit tokens on a trusted server. Do not embed them in a
browser bundle.

## Add a browser payment UI

For a browser-local Fiber node and React components, install the React layer and
the Fiber WASM runtime:

```bash
npm install @fiber-pay/react @nervosnetwork/fiber-js
```

The quickest starting point is `FiberPayQuickCard`:

```tsx
import { FiberPayQuickCard } from "@fiber-pay/react";

export function PaymentPanel() {
  return <FiberPayQuickCard network="testnet" />;
}
```

For a shared node session and more control, compose `useFiberNode`,
`ConnectButton`, and `FiberPayQuickCard`:

```tsx
import {
  ConnectButton,
  FiberPayQuickCard,
  useFiberNode,
} from "@fiber-pay/react";

export function PaymentPanel() {
  const fiber = useFiberNode({
    network: "testnet",
    walletId: "my-app-wallet",
  });

  return (
    <>
      <ConnectButton fiber={fiber} strategy="passkey" />
      <FiberPayQuickCard fiber={fiber} network="testnet" />
    </>
  );
}
```

## Browser requirements

The multithreaded WASM runtime uses `SharedArrayBuffer`. Serve every route that
loads it with these response headers in both development and production:

```text
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
```

<Callout type="info" title="Plan for a large browser chunk">
  The Fiber WASM runtime is much larger than a typical UI dependency. Load
  WASM-dependent payment features lazily or behind an explicit user action so
  the rest of your application does not pay the startup cost.
</Callout>
